To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ebola virus (EVD) disease (EBOVs) circulating in 1977 and 2014 use the same spectrum of host cell receptors, are comparably susceptible for inhibition by cellular interferon-induced trans-membrane proteins and are comparably neutralized by the antibody KZ52, thus suggesting that the EBOVs from both outbreaks should be equally susceptible for antiviral measures targeting the viral glycoprotein and cellular host cell entry factors.

Ebola viruses isolated from patients with Ebola virus disease (EVD), caused by Ebola virus (EboV), in Sierra Leone, 1976 and Zaire, and the United States, 2014 transduced the same spectrum of cells, used the same cellular factors, and were comparably susceptible to inhibition by antiviral IFITMs and KZ52.
Ebola viruses from 1976 and from the ongoing outbreak in 2014 are similar in their ability to enter cells and in their susceptibility to inhibition by antivirals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the host cell entry process of Ebola viruses (EBOV), which is a key event in the viral replication cycle.
the development of a new class of antiviral agents that target the cellular entry of viruses.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of host cell entry of the EBOV circulating in 2014 in Sierra Leone, West Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ebola viruses from 1976 and from 2014 use the same cellular entry factors and are susceptible to the same antiviral strategies.
the Ebola virus from the current outbreak in Western Africa is not more dangerous than the Ebola viruses that have circulated in the past.
the GPs from the EBOV strains from Sierra Leone and Zaire are functionally equivalent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the GPs from 1976 and from 2014 EBOVs are comparably susceptible for inhibition by antiviral mechanisms.
Ebola virus (EboV) from 2014 and 1976 are equally sensitive to antiviral strategies that target the viral glycoprotein and cellular entry factors.
Ebola viruses are similar in their host cell entry mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GPs from the EBOVs from Sierra Leone and Zaire are functionally equivalent, and thus the same cellular entry factors are used by these viruses to enter cells.

the EBOV GPs from the 2014 outbreak and the Zaire strain from the 1976 epidemic are equally dependent on cellular factors for host entry and thus equally susceptible to inhibition by cellular defenses and antiviral therapeutics.

the EBOV GPs from the current and previous epidemics are comparably susceptible toward antiviral strategies, and that the GPs are not likely to have acquired new entry mechanisms that would require new antiviral strategies.
